title: Official HTTPS Evidence Provenance & Verification Policy
objective: Establish a scientifically defensible, multi-tier provenance trust model distinguishing official authenticated HTTPS acquisition from publisher document signatures, local files, and untrusted sources.

Level_A.name: VERIFIED_PUBLISHER_SIGNATURE
Level_A.description: Document-level digital signature verified against a trusted publisher signing key (e.g. GPG/PGP attestation).

Level_B.name: VERIFIED_OFFICIAL_HTTPS_ACQUISITION
Level_B.description: Document acquired through an authenticated HTTPS session from an explicitly allowlisted official publisher endpoint.
Level_B.governance_rule: HTTPS acquisition provenance must never be promoted or misclassified as a publisher document signature.

Level_C.name: SOURCE_CLAIMED_OFFICIAL
Level_C.description: Local file, manual entry, or document claiming official publisher origin without verifiable acquisition provenance.
Level_C.treatment: Cannot independently satisfy official schedule authenticity; retains candidate/unverified status.

Level_D.name: SOURCE_UNTRUSTED
Level_D.description: Unknown, altered, conflicting, unsafe, or unauthorized evidence.
Level_D.treatment: Must be rejected or quarantined immediately.

acceptance_criteria.dual_track_acceptance: Either Level A (VERIFIED_PUBLISHER_SIGNATURE) or Level B (VERIFIED_OFFICIAL_HTTPS_ACQUISITION) independently satisfies official source authenticity.
acceptance_criteria.strict_isolation: Client-provided claims of TLS success are rejected; only trusted acquisition component can generate Level B provenance.
acceptance_criteria.immutability: Acquired evidence must be immutably hashed and vaulted with no silent upgrade of historical evidence.
